description: Renovate settings shared across kanso-labs, extended as local>kanso-labs/.github:renovate-config by the runner's config.js and by every repository that ships a config of its own. It is listed after config:recommended so these values win, and it deliberately extends nothing itself: a preset that pulled in config:recommended would reinstate it for a consumer that had chosen otherwise. Everything here was previously restated in each repository, byte for byte; a setting only some repositories want does not belong here, because a consumer cannot opt out of a preset it extends except by restating the opposite. dependencyDashboard is off because nothing in this organization holds an update back, so every pending update is already an open pull request and the dashboard would do nothing but restate them.

packageRules.description: Renovate's own config:recommended sets semanticCommitType through a packageRule, and packageRules beat top-level config. Setting it at the top level therefore does nothing at all: every upgrade stays chore and cuts no release. This rule is first so that a repository's own rules can still override it for specific packages, which home-assistant-applications relies on to type container bumps as fix.

Updates from the github-actions manager are typed ci, which every repository's release-please config hides except kanso-labs/actions', so bumping one cuts no release. That manager reads only workflow and action definitions, which a package, an app or an add-on never ships. Typed deps, a bump of kanso-labs/actions alone opened react-native-kanso-ui's 0.16.9, whose notes said nothing but that. Regex managers aimed at .github/workflows are deliberately left deps: the tool one pins can shape what a repository ships, as react-native-daily's eas-cli publishes its updates, and a repository whose pins never do can type them itself. A group that mixes an update from this manager with a package's, as home-assistant-robot-vacuum-map's Home Assistant group does with the hassfest image, takes whichever type comes first; both are hidden there, so it releases nothing either way. kanso-labs/actions is the exception, because its workflows and composite actions are what consumers pin, so its own config restates deps for this manager and, landing after this rule, wins. It follows the deps rule above so that it wins, and a repository's own rules still land after it.

Development tooling that never reaches what a repository ships — linters, formatters, commit and hook tooling, test runners and package checks — is typed chore, which every repository's release-please config hides, so bumping it cuts no release. Typed deps, a typescript-eslint bump alone opened kanso-ui-core's 0.1.24, and lint tooling alone cut 0.1.20 to 0.1.23. It matches npm devDependencies only, so a package a repository ships, or names as a peer, stays deps. Build tooling that shapes the published output, such as tsdown, typescript and style-dictionary, is deliberately absent and stays deps. eslint-plugin-storybook is negated because kanso-ui groups it with Storybook, and a group whose upgrades disagree on the type takes whichever comes first. It follows the deps rule above so that it wins, and a repository's own rules still land after it.

Minors, patches and lock file maintenance automerge. Lock file maintenance is an update type of its own, which a rule for minors and patches does not reach, so it is named here rather than left to each repository's lockFileMaintenance block: until it was, the repositories that never restated automerge there left its pull request waiting for a person every day. A repository that needs a human on a particular package states a narrower rule in its own config, which lands after this one and therefore wins — actions does exactly that for rhysd/actionlint.
